title: Doing No Harm
note: This means not harming any being, whether for gain, out of hatred or through carelessness. Harm happens without anger too, so it follows the chapter on anger.

couplets.plain: Doing no harm to others, even for wealth that brings high standing, is the rule of those without stain.
couplets.pm: Even if harming others could win the eight powers, such as becoming tiny, that give the distinction of yoga, those pure in mind by the scriptures’ measure are resolved not to do it. They are free of the stains of desire, anger and delusion. This forbids harm done for your own gain.

links.quote: Doing no harm to others, even for wealth that brings high standing
links.reason: Keeps the rule even with wealth and high standing as the prize for breaking it.

couplets.plain: Not harming in return, even when someone has harmed you in hatred, is the rule of those without stain.
couplets.pm: Even when someone bears them a grudge and harms them, those pure in mind are resolved not to harm back. What they should do is let the harm go and not take it to heart.
couplets.sensitive: counsels not answering injury done in hate

links.quote: even when someone has harmed you in hatred
links.reason: Holds the rule against the hardest case, harm done in hatred.
Makes refusing to harm in return the settled rule of the stainless, whatever was done to them.

couplets.plain: If you harm even those who hated you when you had done nothing to them, it brings you misery you can’t escape.
couplets.pm: You have done no harm, yet someone bears you a grudge. If you have renounced and still harm even them, the act brings you trouble you can’t get past: you lose your penance and gain blame and sin.
couplets.sensitive: warns an unprovoked victim against hitting back

links.quote: those who hated you when you had done nothing to them
links.reason: Extends the ban to one who hated you without cause.
Puts the cost of paying back on the one who does it: misery that can’t be escaped.

couplets.plain: The way to punish those who harm you is to do them such good that they are ashamed, and then let it go.
couplets.pm: For those who have renounced, punishing someone who harms them means doing that person such kindness that they are ashamed, then forgetting both the harm and the kindness. Remembered, these would come back and grow. This is the way to defeat them.
couplets.sensitive: tells the injured to repay harm with kindness

links.quote: do them such good that they are ashamed
such good that they are ashamed
The way to punish those who harm you

couplets.plain: What good is your understanding, if you don’t guard against another’s pain as you would your own?
couplets.pm: What use to those who have renounced is their true knowledge of living beings, if they don’t guard others from harm as they would guard themselves? Guarding means foreseeing what walking, sitting, lying, standing and eating may do to creatures, above all tiny ones, and keeping them safe. This forbids harm done through carelessness.

links.quote: guard against another’s pain as you would your own
links.reason: Rates understanding as useless unless it guards against another’s pain as its own.

couplets.plain: What you know to be painful, you must not do to anyone else.
couplets.pm: Those who have renounced must not do to another what they have worked out is painful to people. Pleasure and pain belong to the soul and can’t be seen directly, so this knowledge comes by inference. It says “know” because righteousness and sin arise only where the mind is present.

links.quote: you must not do to anyone else
links.reason: Turns what you know of pain into a rule: don’t do it to anyone else.

couplets.plain: Doing no wilful harm, in any measure, at any time, to anyone, is the highest thing.
couplets.pm: The highest righteousness is never to do harm that comes with the mind’s consent, to anyone, at any time, however small. Without the mind there is no sin. “Any time” means even when you have power, “anyone” means even the weak, and “in any measure” because even a small act is a great sin.

links.quote: Doing no wilful harm, in any measure, at any time, to anyone

couplets.plain: You know what harm feels like to your own life. Why, then, do you harm other lives?
couplets.pm: You have felt what harm from others does to your own life. For what reason, then, do you do it to other enduring lives? You can infer that it hurts them too, and the scriptures say such harm comes back to torment you. The only reason you don’t stop is delusion.

links.quote: Why, then, do you harm other lives
links.reason: Asks in disbelief how anyone who knows harm firsthand can do it to others.

couplets.plain: Harm others in the morning, and harm will come to you in the afternoon, by itself.
couplets.pm: If those who have renounced harm others in the first part of a day, harm comes to them in the later part of it, by itself, without their doing anything. Their penance is ruined, so it comes quickly and easily. So don’t do it.

links.quote: harm will come to you in the afternoon, by itself
links.reason: Compresses the return of a deed into one day: harm in the morning, harm in the afternoon.

couplets.plain: All pain falls on those who cause pain. Those who want to be free of pain cause none.
couplets.pm: All harm falls on those who harm another being, since whoever sows deeds reaps that same crop. So those who want no harm for themselves do none to any other.

links.quote: All pain falls on those who cause pain
links.reason: States the law at its widest: all pain falls back on the one who caused it.

links.quote: Those who want to be free of pain cause none
